app.run: This repository is a library without an app of its own; its UI (the connect button and connection panel in src/ui) shows in calliope-campus, which imports it. To see a change there, run `node .obeya/campus-host.mjs start` in your workspace (in the background; it takes about a minute the first time). It clones the campus checkout beside this repository (editors/calliope-campus in the calliope-dev superrepo, at its current HEAD) into D:/tmp/mcw-campus-host/<workspace>/, links that clone's widget to your workspace, installs it and starts campus's Vite dev server on the first free port from 5300; it prints the URL (also in D:/tmp/mcw-campus-host/<workspace>/dev.url, log in dev.log next to it). Edits under src/ reload in the browser by themselves (Vite HMR); `node .obeya/campus-host.mjs status` prints the URL while it runs. campus at its HEAD expects the widget's current main branch: a blank page with a "does not provide an export named …" error in the browser console means the workspace's branch is behind it (rebase onto main). Open `<url>makecode?debug=1`: the standalone MakeCode editor (it loads makecode.calliope.cc; no login, no backend), with the widget's connect button at the top right; `?debug=1` turns on its advanced view. /python and /blocks show the same widget, but /blocks with `?debug=1` points its editor frame at a local Blocks editor (https://localhost:8601) that is not running, so the frame stays empty. The first load after a start reloads itself once or twice while Vite optimizes dependencies; wait for the page to settle. HTTPS uses the campus checkout's locally trusted certificate (certs/, valid for 127.0.0.1); without one there, campus falls back to a self-signed one and a headless browser has to ignore certificate errors. A headless browser cannot pair a real Calliope mini over WebUSB or Bluetooth: a demo shows the widget's UI and its states without a device. `node .obeya/campus-host.mjs stop` stops the server (by its PID) and removes the scratch clone.
